title: The pleasure of eating alone
paragraphs: Should you eat to live or live to eat?... a question posed by French playwright Moliere in his work ‘The Miser’. While eating is functional, and our bodies need the fuel that food provides, dining with friends or loved ones can be a wonderful experience. However, some of us often find ourselves reserving a table for one in a restaurant. But is dining alone really that bad? Maybe not.

We all have foods we like and dislike. Maybe it’s a pungent cheese or stinky fish. We sometimes hold back on things that may offend the noses of others. When dining alone, we can consume whatever we like, with the added bonus that we might be able to eat more healthily. Often, if you want a salad and your significant other wants some less healthy cuisine, you end up ordering the same. And if you don’t get the same, you might end up with food envy as you watch someone chow down on a pizza while you’re left holding the lettuce.

Have you ever spent too long debating with people which restaurant to eat in or when to meet? If dining solo, you can make the choice depending on your culinary desires at that moment and get your nourishment at exactly the time you’re hungry! And why does it have to be a restaurant? You could eat in a park, garden or even your bed – the point is, the choice is yours! That alone time also means it’s a time to switch off. According to psychologist Sherrie Bourg Carter, a bit of solitude can help your brain to unwind and may help you concentrate more.

Finally, for some, dining alone can be a necessity. For those of us who suffer from misophonia, a hatred of sound, that can in some cause PTSD, the noise of someone else masticating can be unbearable. Eating alone can save you from the extreme anxiety that may arise listening to someone smack their lips or the sloshing of saliva in their mouths! So, is eating alone bad? Well, it may not be for everyone, but there certainly are some benefits to it. Try it sometime – you might just like it!

vocabulary.entry: pose /pəʊz/ v. 提出（问题、观点等）
vocabulary.example: The philosopher posed a series of questions about human nature.
vocabulary.translation: 这位哲学家提出了一系列关于人性的问题。

vocabulary.entry: playwright /ˈpleɪraɪt/ n. 剧作家
vocabulary.example: The young playwright's new work was well received by critics.
vocabulary.translation: 这位青年剧作家的新作受到了评论家的好评。

vocabulary.entry: functional /ˈfʌŋkʃənl/ adj. 具有实用功能的；实用的
vocabulary.example: The room's design is simple and functional.
vocabulary.translation: 这个房间的设计简洁又实用。

vocabulary.entry: fuel /ˈfjuːəl/ n. 能量来源；燃料
vocabulary.example: Fruits and vegetables are important fuel for our bodies.
vocabulary.translation: 果蔬是我们身体重要的能量来源。

vocabulary.entry: reserve /rɪˈzɜːv/ v. 预订（座位、房间等）
vocabulary.example: I need to reserve a table for two at the restaurant tonight.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要在这家餐厅预订今晚的双人桌。

vocabulary.entry: pungent /ˈpʌndʒənt/ adj. 气味浓烈的；刺鼻的
vocabulary.example: The pungent smell of garlic filled the kitchen.
vocabulary.translation: 厨房里弥漫着大蒜刺鼻的气味。

vocabulary.entry: stinky /ˈstɪŋki/ adj. 有臭味的；难闻的
vocabulary.example: The stinky tofu is a popular snack in some Asian countries.
vocabulary.translation: 臭豆腐在一些亚洲国家是很受欢迎的小吃。

vocabulary.entry: hold back /həʊld bæk/ 克制；抑制（情感、欲望等）
vocabulary.example: She had to hold back her tears during the speech.
vocabulary.translation: 演讲时她不得不忍住眼泪。

vocabulary.entry: offend /əˈfend/ v. 使不适；冒犯
vocabulary.example: The strong smell might offend some sensitive people.
vocabulary.translation: 这种浓烈的气味可能会让一些敏感的人感到不适。

vocabulary.entry: consume /kənˈsjuːm/ v. 吃；饮用
vocabulary.example: We should consume more fresh produce for a healthy diet.
vocabulary.translation: 为了健康饮食，我们应该多吃新鲜农产品。

vocabulary.entry: added bonus /ˈædɪd ˈbəʊnəs/ 额外的好处；附加福利
vocabulary.example: Learning a new language has the added bonus of broadening your horizons.
vocabulary.translation: 学习一门新语言还有拓展视野的额外好处。

vocabulary.entry: significant other /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt ˈʌðə/ 伴侣；另一半
vocabulary.example: Her significant other surprised her with a birthday gift.
vocabulary.translation: 她的伴侣给了她一个生日惊喜。

vocabulary.entry: cuisine /kwɪˈziːn/ n. 菜肴；烹饪风格
vocabulary.example: Italian cuisine is famous for its pasta and pizza.
vocabulary.translation: 意大利菜以其面食和披萨而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: food envy /fuːd ˈenvi/ n. 美食羡慕
vocabulary.example: She felt a twinge of food envy when she saw her friend's dessert.
vocabulary.translation: 看到朋友的甜点，她心里涌起一阵小小的美食羡慕。

vocabulary.entry: chow down /tʃaʊ daʊn/ （非正式）狼吞虎咽地吃；大快朵颐
vocabulary.example: We chowed down on the delicious barbecue at the picnic.
vocabulary.translation: 野餐时我们狼吞虎咽地吃着美味的烧烤。

vocabulary.entry: debate /dɪˈbeɪt/ v. 争论；讨论
vocabulary.example: The team debated for hours about the best way to solve the problem.
vocabulary.translation: 团队为解决问题的最佳方案争论了好几个小时。

vocabulary.entry: solo /ˈsəʊləʊ/ adj. 独自的；单独的
vocabulary.example: She took a solo trip around Europe last summer.
vocabulary.translation: 去年夏天她独自环游了欧洲。

vocabulary.entry: culinary desire /ˈkʌlɪnəri dɪˈzaɪə/ 饮食欲望；想吃东西的念头
vocabulary.example: Her culinary desire for spicy food made her order a hot pot.
vocabulary.translation: 她想吃辣的欲望让她点了火锅。

vocabulary.entry: nourishment /ˈnʌrɪʃmənt/ n. 营养；滋养品
vocabulary.example: The soup provides rich nourishment for the sick.
vocabulary.translation: 这款汤能为病人提供丰富的营养。

vocabulary.entry: switch off /swɪtʃ ɒf/ 放松身心；不再思考烦心事
vocabulary.example: I like to switch off by listening to music after work.
vocabulary.translation: 下班后我喜欢听音乐来放松身心。

vocabulary.entry: solitude /ˈsɒlɪtjuːd/ n. 独处；独居
vocabulary.example: She enjoyed the solitude of the countryside.
vocabulary.translation: 她很享受乡村的独处时光。

vocabulary.entry: unwind /ˌʌnˈwaɪnd/ v. 放松；舒缓
vocabulary.example: Reading a book is a great way to unwind after a busy day.
vocabulary.translation: 忙碌一天后，看书是很好的放松方式。

vocabulary.entry: misophonia /ˌmaɪsəˈfəʊniə/ n. 恐音症
vocabulary.example: People with misophonia may feel annoyed by the sound of chewing.
vocabulary.translation: 恐音症患者可能会对咀嚼声感到烦躁。

vocabulary.entry: masticate /ˈmæstɪkeɪt/ v. 咀嚼；嚼碎
vocabulary.example: It is important to masticate food thoroughly before swallowing.
vocabulary.translation: 吞咽前充分咀嚼食物很重要。

vocabulary.entry: slosh /slɒʃ/ v. （液体）晃动发出声响
vocabulary.example: The water sloshed in the bucket as he carried it.
vocabulary.translation: 他提着水桶时，桶里的水晃来晃去发出声响。

sentences.english: Should you eat to live or live to eat?... a question posed by French playwright Moliere in his work ‘The Miser’.
sentences.chinese: 人应该为了活着而吃饭，还是为了吃饭而活着？这是法国剧作家莫里哀在其作品《吝啬鬼》中提出的问题。

sentences.english: While eating is functional, and our bodies need the fuel that food provides, dining with friends or loved ones can be a wonderful experience.
sentences.chinese: 吃饭固然具有实际功用，我们的身体也需要食物提供的能量，但与亲友一同用餐，也可以是一段十分美好的经历。

sentences.english: However, some of us often find ourselves reserving a table for one in a restaurant.
sentences.chinese: 不过，我们中有些人却常常会在餐厅里预订单人餐桌。

sentences.english: But is dining alone really that bad?
sentences.chinese: 但独自用餐真的有那么糟糕吗？

sentences.english: Maybe not.
sentences.chinese: 或许并非如此。

sentences.english: We all have foods we like and dislike. Maybe it’s a pungent cheese or stinky fish.
sentences.chinese: 每个人都有自己爱吃和不爱吃的东西，可能是气味浓烈的奶酪，也可能是腥味很重的鱼。

sentences.english: We sometimes hold back on things that may offend the noses of others.
sentences.chinese: 有些食物可能会让别人觉得刺鼻，我们有时就会克制自己不去吃。

sentences.english: When dining alone, we can consume whatever we like, with the added bonus that we might be able to eat more healthily.
sentences.chinese: 但独自用餐时，你可以随心所欲地吃任何想吃的东西，而且还有一个额外的好处——你或许能吃得更健康。

sentences.english: Often, if you want a salad and your significant other wants some less healthy cuisine, you end up ordering the same.
sentences.chinese: 很多时候，如果你想吃沙拉，而你的伴侣却想吃些没那么健康的菜肴，最后你们很可能会点一样的东西。

sentences.english: And if you don’t get the same, you might end up with food envy as you watch someone chow down on a pizza while you’re left holding the lettuce.
sentences.chinese: 就算你们点的不一样，看着别人大快朵颐地吃着披萨，自己却只能啃着生菜，你也可能会产生“美食羡慕”的心情。

sentences.english: Have you ever spent too long debating with people which restaurant to eat in or when to meet?
sentences.chinese: 你是否曾和别人花了很长时间争论去哪家餐厅吃饭、什么时候碰面？

sentences.english: If dining solo, you can make the choice depending on your culinary desires at that moment and get your nourishment at exactly the time you’re hungry!
sentences.chinese: 如果是独自用餐，你可以完全根据当下的饮食欲望做决定，在自己饿的时候准时补充营养！

sentences.english: And why does it have to be a restaurant?
sentences.chinese: 而且为什么非得去餐厅呢？

sentences.english: You could eat in a park, garden or even your bed – the point is, the choice is yours!
sentences.chinese: 你可以去公园、花园，甚至在床上吃——关键是，选择权在你自己手里！

sentences.english: That alone time also means it’s a time to switch off.
sentences.chinese: 这段独处的时光，也是一段能让你彻底放松的时光。

sentences.english: According to psychologist Sherrie Bourg Carter, a bit of solitude can help your brain to unwind and may help you concentrate more.
sentences.chinese: 心理学家雪莉·伯格·卡特表示，适度的独处有助于大脑放松，还能提升专注力。

sentences.english: Finally, for some, dining alone can be a necessity.
sentences.chinese: 最后，对有些人来说，独自用餐是一种必需。

sentences.english: For those of us who suffer from misophonia, a hatred of sound, that can in some cause PTSD, the noise of someone else masticating can be unbearable.
sentences.chinese: 对于患有恐音症（一种对特定声音的厌恶感，严重时可能会引发创伤后应激障碍）的人而言，别人咀嚼食物的声音会让他们难以忍受。

sentences.english: Eating alone can save you from the extreme anxiety that may arise listening to someone smack their lips or the sloshing of saliva in their mouths!
sentences.chinese: 独自用餐可以让他们免受煎熬——不用再因为听到别人咂嘴或是口腔里唾液晃动的声音而陷入极度焦虑！

sentences.english: So, is eating alone bad?
sentences.chinese: 所以，独自用餐真的不好吗？

sentences.english: Well, it may not be for everyone, but there certainly are some benefits to it.
sentences.chinese: 当然，它可能并不适合所有人，但确实有不少好处。

sentences.english: Try it sometime – you might just like it!
sentences.chinese: 不妨找个时间试试看——说不定你会喜欢上这种方式呢！
